were examined in relation to incident risk of colon and rectal cancer over a median follow-up of 10.6 years (Egeberg et al., 2010).
Among 26,630 men, there were 461 incident cases of colon cancer and the incident relative risk (IRR) per 50 g of whole grain intake
was 0.85 (95% CI 0.77, 0.94). There were 283 incident cases of rectal cancer with an IRR of 0.90 (95% CI 0.80, 1.01). There were no
consistent associations between total or individual whole grain consumption and colon or rectal cancer risk among women. In men,
